question: According to the phase-in schedule in Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11, what was the maximum qualifying age requiring a California Boater Card beginning January 1, 2019?
choice_a: 25 and younger
explanation: The statutory phase-in raised the age threshold each year: 20 and younger in 2018, then 25 and younger starting January 1, 2019.
source_note: CA Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11, phase-in schedule (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)

question: Under the Boater Card phase-in schedule, operators age 40 and younger became required to hold the card beginning in which year?
explanation: The statutory schedule required operators 40 and younger to hold a card starting January 1, 2021, one step in the annual expansion toward covering all ages by 2025.
source_note: CA Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11, phase-in schedule (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)

question: By January 1, 2023, the Boater Card requirement had expanded to cover operators up to what age?
choice_a: 45 and younger
explanation: The phase-in schedule set the threshold at 50 and younger effective January 1, 2023, the year before it jumped to 60 and younger.
source_note: CA Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11, phase-in schedule (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)

question: In 2024, the year before the Boater Card requirement covered all operators regardless of age, which operators became newly required to carry the card?
choice_a: Those 50 and younger
explanation: The final phase-in step before universal coverage set the threshold at 60 and younger, effective January 1, 2024; the requirement then applied to every age starting January 1, 2025.
source_note: CA Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11, phase-in schedule (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)

question: Separate from the Boater Card mandate itself, what is the general minimum age to operate a vessel powered by a motor in California?
choice_a: 16 years old, while also possessing a valid California Boater Card
choice_d: There is no minimum age to operate a motorized vessel
explanation: California sets 16 as the general minimum age to operate a motor-powered vessel, and that operator must also possess a valid California Boater Card.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Operator Age and Education Requirements"

question: Under what condition may a 12- to 15-year-old legally operate a motorized vessel with more than 15 horsepower, including a personal watercraft, in California?
choice_a: Never, regardless of supervision
choice_b: Only with on-board supervision by a person at least 18 years old who holds a valid California Boater Card
choice_c: Only if the vessel is registered in the minor's own name
explanation: California allows 12- to 15-year-olds to operate a motorized vessel over 15 horsepower, including a PWC, only when a card-holding adult at least 18 years old is on board supervising.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Operator Age and Education Requirements"

question: California's age restriction on operating a motorized vessel does NOT apply to which type of vessel?
choice_a: A personal watercraft under 30 feet long
choice_c: A sailboat under 30 feet long using wind as its main source of propulsion
explanation: There is no age restriction for operating a sailboat under 30 feet long when wind is the main source of propulsion.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Operator Age and Education Requirements"

question: Under Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11, operating a vessel in which of the following activities is exempt from the California Boater Card requirement?
choice_a: A fishing tournament with no organized racing
choice_b: An informal dinner cruise chartered among friends
choice_d: An organized regatta, vessel race, or water ski race
explanation: The statute exempts a person operating a vessel in an organized regatta, vessel race, or water ski race from needing a Boater Card during that activity.
source_note: CA Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11(c)(3) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)

question: Which credential exempts its holder from needing a separate California Boater Card while actively using it?
choice_a: A current commercial fishing license
choice_d: A California State Parks annual day-use pass
explanation: A person in possession of a current commercial fishing license is statutorily exempt from the Boater Card requirement.
source_note: CA Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11(c)(5) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)

question: A person holding a valid marine operator license issued by the U.S. Coast Guard, or a valid certificate under the international STCW convention, is exempt from what California requirement?
choice_a: The vessel registration requirement
choice_d: The use tax on vessel purchases
explanation: Holders of a valid USCG marine operator license or a valid STCW certificate are exempt from having to also carry a California Boater Card.
source_note: CA Harbors and Navigation Code Section 678.11(c)(6) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov)

question: Under California law, when is a vessel operator ordered by a court to complete a DBW-approved boating safety course?
choice_a: Automatically upon first-time vessel registration
choice_b: Only if the operator is under age 25
choice_c: Upon conviction of a moving violation under the Harbors and Navigation Code, the Federal Rules of the Road, or DBW regulations while operating a vessel
explanation: Anyone convicted of a moving violation under the Harbors and Navigation Code, Federal Rules of the Road, or DBW regulations while operating a vessel must be ordered by the court to complete and pass a DBW-approved boating safety course.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Court-Ordered Boating Education"

question: After a court orders boating education following a qualifying conviction, how long does the operator have to submit proof of course completion to the court?
choice_a: 30 days from the date of conviction
choice_b: One year from the date of conviction
choice_d: Seven months from the date of conviction
explanation: Proof of completing and passing the court-ordered course must be submitted to the court within seven months of the conviction date.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Court-Ordered Boating Education"

question: Which of these vessels is exempt from California's registration requirement because it is manually propelled?
choice_a: A rowboat moved only by oars
choice_d: A sail-assisted kayak fitted with an auxiliary gas motor
explanation: Manually propelled vessels, such as a rowboat moved only by oars, are exempt from California's vessel registration requirement.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Which Boats Require Registration?"

question: A sailboard or small sailboat is exempt from California vessel registration if it is propelled solely by sail and is no longer than what length?
choice_a: 12 feet
explanation: Sailboards and other vessels 8 feet or less in length that are propelled solely by sail are exempt from registration.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Which Boats Require Registration?"

question: Which vessel type is specifically exempt from California registration because it is used solely for life-saving purposes?
choice_a: A rental pontoon boat
explanation: Ship's lifeboats used solely for life-saving purposes are among the vessel types exempt from California registration.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Which Boats Require Registration?"

question: A vessel already validly registered in another state remains exempt from California registration as long as it is not kept in California for more than how many consecutive days?
choice_a: 30 days
explanation: An out-of-state registered vessel is exempt from California registration only while it is not kept in California for more than 90 consecutive days; this is distinct from the 60-day exemption that applies to an out-of-state operator's Boater Card requirement.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Which Boats Require Registration?"

question: When the California DMV registers a vessel, what set of documents does it issue to the owner?
choice_a: A Certificate of Number, a Certificate of Ownership, and registration stickers
choice_c: A title only, with stickers issued separately by DBW
choice_d: A Boater Card and a Certificate of Ownership
explanation: Upon registering a vessel, the DMV issues a Certificate of Number (registration certificate), a Certificate of Ownership, and a set of registration stickers.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Certificate of Number (Registration Certificate)"

question: California law requires a vessel's Certificate of Number to be available in what way whenever the vessel is in use?
choice_a: Filed only with the DMV and not required aboard
choice_b: On board and available for inspection by an enforcement officer
choice_c: Displayed publicly on a dock placard
choice_d: Available only upon written request within 30 days
explanation: The Certificate of Number must be on board and available for inspection by an enforcement officer whenever the vessel is in use.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Certificate of Number (Registration Certificate)"

question: A California vessel's Certificate of Number is normally valid for two years, except when it is originally issued under what circumstance, which makes it valid for only one year?
choice_a: When it is issued to a first-time owner
choice_b: When the vessel is under 16 feet
choice_c: When it is issued in an odd-numbered year
choice_d: When it is issued for a documented vessel
explanation: A Certificate of Number is valid for two years unless it is issued in an odd-numbered year, in which case it is valid for only one year -- consistent with registrations expiring December 31 of odd-numbered years.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Other Facts About Titling and Registering Your Boat"

question: What is the function of the reverse side of a California vessel's Certificate of Ownership?
choice_a: It lists the vessel's full maintenance history
choice_b: It is blank and reserved for DMV internal use only
choice_c: It records the vessel's insurance policy number
choice_d: It serves as the application for transfer of ownership
explanation: The reverse side of the Certificate of Ownership is itself the application form used to transfer ownership to a new owner.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Other Facts About Titling and Registering Your Boat"

question: A use tax may apply to a California-registered vessel in which situation?
choice_a: When it was acquired out-of-state or purchased from a private party
choice_b: Whenever a registration is renewed on schedule
choice_c: Only when a vessel is scrapped
explanation: California may apply a use tax, calculated on the purchase price, to a vessel that was acquired out-of-state or bought from a private seller.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Other Facts About Titling and Registering Your Boat"

question: Within how many days must a California vessel owner notify the DMV, surrendering the Certificate of Number and Certificate of Ownership, if the vessel is destroyed or abandoned?
choice_a: 5 days
explanation: The DMV must be notified within 15 days of a vessel's destruction or abandonment, along with surrender of the Certificate of Number and Certificate of Ownership.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Other Facts About Titling and Registering Your Boat"

question: Within how many days must a California vessel owner notify the DMV of a change of address?
choice_a: 5 days
explanation: A California vessel owner must notify the DMV of a change of address within 15 days.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Other Facts About Titling and Registering Your Boat"

question: Within how many calendar days of selling a vessel must a California owner notify the DMV, providing the date of sale, a description of the vessel, and the new owner's name and address?
choice_a: 15 calendar days
explanation: Sale notice must be provided to the DMV within five calendar days and must include the date of sale, a description of the vessel, and the new owner's name and address.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Other Facts About Titling and Registering Your Boat"

question: A vessel documented with the U.S. Coast Guard, though exempt from CF numbering, must display what on its stern above the waterline?
choice_a: The vessel's name and hailing port
explanation: A federally documented vessel must display its name and hailing port on the stern above the waterline, even though it is exempt from CF numbering.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Other Facts About Titling and Registering Your Boat"

question: On a California vessel's registration number display, how must the letters be separated from the numbers?
choice_a: They may not be separated at all
choice_b: By a space or hyphen, for example CF 5573 JS or CF-5573-JS
explanation: The letters of the CF number must be separated from the numbers by a space or hyphen, such as CF 5573 JS or CF-5573-JS, and no other numbers may be displayed near it.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Displaying the Registration Number and Validation Decals"

question: Boaters operating on California's freshwater lakes and reservoirs must display which additional decal, positioned behind the registration validation sticker, that is not required for saltwater-only boating?
choice_a: A second CF number decal
choice_d: A duplicate Hull Identification Number plate
explanation: Freshwater boating in California requires a Quagga/Zebra Mussel fee sticker, affixed on both sides of the bow behind and in line with the registration validation sticker.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Displaying the Registration Number and Validation Decals"

question: What is a Hull Identification Number (HIN) on a California vessel?
choice_a: A number assigned annually by the DMV upon registration renewal
choice_b: The same number as the CF registration number
choice_c: An optional number vessel owners may create themselves
choice_d: A unique 12-digit number assigned by the manufacturer to vessels built after 1972
explanation: The HIN is a unique 12-digit number assigned by the manufacturer to vessels built after 1972, serving the same identifying purpose as a vehicle serial number.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Hull Identification Numbers"

question: Where is a vessel's Hull Identification Number (HIN) physically located?
choice_a: Engraved in the fiberglass or on a metal plate permanently attached to the transom
choice_b: Printed on the Certificate of Number only
explanation: The HIN is engraved in the fiberglass or on a metal plate permanently attached to the vessel's transom.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Hull Identification Numbers"

question: Why does California's boating safety course recommend that owners record their HIN somewhere separate from the vessel itself?
choice_a: Because the number must be re-engraved every two years
choice_b: So the number is still available for reference if the vessel is stolen or warranty problems arise
choice_c: Because HINs are automatically removed after registration is complete
choice_d: Because the HIN doubles as the owner's DMV PIN
explanation: Owners are advised to write down their HIN and keep it separate from the vessel in case the vessel is stolen or warranty problems arise.
source_note: Boat-Ed California Study Guide, "Hull Identification Numbers"
